ai_answer: The Supreme Court has held that Article 21 protects a broad spectrum of rights that together constitute the right to life and personal liberty.  It is not limited to mere physical survival but includes the dignity, privacy, freedom of movement, and the right to live with human dignity.  The Court has repeatedly emphasized that no person can be deprived of life or personal liberty except in accordance with a law that is fair, reasonable and procedurally fair.  The right is a fundamental right that is protected by the Constitution and is enforceable through Article 32 and Article 226.  The Court has also clarified that Article 21 is not the sole repository of the right to life and personal liberty, but it is the primary constitutional safeguard for these rights.

question: freedom of speech and reasonable restrictions under Article 19

top_3_cases.title: KAUSHAL KISHOR versus STATE OF UTTAR PRADESH & ORS.
LIFE INSURANCE CORPN. OF INDIA AND ORS. ETC. versus PROF. MANUBHAI D. SHAH ETC. ETC.
INDIAN EXPRESS NEWSPAPERS (BOMBAY) PRIVATE LTD. & ORS. ETC. ETC.  versus UNION OF INDIA & ORS. ETC. ETC .

ai_answer: The Supreme Court has held that the right to freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a) is not absolute; it is subject to reasonable restrictions enumerated in Article 19(2).  The Court has repeatedly emphasized that any restriction must be grounded in the categories listed in Article 19(2) – such as sovereignty and integrity of India, security of the state, friendly relations with foreign states, public order, decency or morality, contempt of court, defamation, or incitement to violence – and must be reasonable and proportionate.  Speech that falls outside the protective perimeter of Article 19(1)(a) – for example hate speech, defamatory speech, or speech that directly conflicts with the rights of others – may be restrained without invoking Article 19(2).  Thus, the State may impose restrictions on speech only when they are justified by one of the enumerated grounds and are reasonable in the circumstances.
